commits.message: docs(evidence,ledger): seal the #617 wave — p8 addendum20260823 and the wave-seal GOAL_PROGRESS rows (#617, #623, #628, #633)

docs(evidence): name the axis on the l2_datum width claim and the pattern-source branch (#628, #617)

The ledger note and the one-byte rung's infeasibility both said the wider
rungs add 'under 720K mem' without naming which axis that is. It holds on
the marginal axis (717,375 across the 1-byte to 256-byte rungs); the
whole-test span across the same rungs is +1,533,414 because fixture growth
is charged to the row. Both sentences now say so.

The verifier header cited verify-native-script-scan-exec-ledger-v1.mjs as
its pattern source, which reads as an in-tree sibling but exists only on
the unmerged wave/lane-l branch pending the owner's #633 ruling. Cite the
branch instead.

The C53 row's expectedNonzeroCounts and blockedBecause still narrated the

stale clauses are retained verbatim and a dated addendum records the
122-row registry (14+90+14+4; 17 additions, 0 removals, measured set
unchanged at 10), the 112-row unfit pin, and the 4/4 suite result with

byte-identical to the pre-edit baseline (186/186 tasks, the same 9
pre-existing defects), verified against the unedited parent manifest.

row identity: exactly 17 additions -- prepare[12], prepare[13], and
semantic[75..89] -- exactly 0 removals, and the measured set unchanged at
10 rows (same ten category/index keys, all still genuinely

re-derives the whole sweep through the real emulator lifecycle and

The inline-flip journey staged a 12,900-byte payload, sized to sit just

the journey failed to stage at all. Stage 13,100 instead: the item lands

evidence(transition-trace,descriptor): gate the #628 ExUnits frontier and measure both crossings (#628, #617)

The #628 frontier evidence could not answer the question it was written for.
Aiken reports whole-test execution units, so every transition-trace row charged
its own MPF-root and CBOR fixture construction to the reading, and the basis
crossing for descriptor derivation was interpolated between two golden vectors
of different shape rather than measured. Both defects put a sign-off figure
beyond re-checking.

Replace the ungated artifact with a gated exec ledger on the lane-l pattern,
plus the two things it needs to be evidence:

* Programmatic sweep vectors in two new test modules -- payloads built by a
  doubling builder, never as source literals -- pairing every measured arm row
  with a fixture-only twin built by the same builder. The verifier recomputes
  each difference, so a marginal cost is arithmetic over pinned rows rather
  than prose.
* A lane verifier that judges basisFit in both directions, requires an
  infeasibility and a ruling on every over-basis row, recomputes every marginal
  figure and every crossing bracket, refuses a crossing that is not adjacent
  and refuses an interpolation on a dimension a measurement already covers.
  It imports the basis and the reading path from the shared modules and leaves
  exec-ledger-within-basis-v1.mjs untouched.

The measurements change two published claims. Descriptor derivation crosses the
basis between 2,687 and 2,753 output bytes, not the ~1,680 the interpolation
gave: that slope folded the rich vector's asset and reference-script cost into
its size cost. And net of fixture cost neither repointed arm is over the basis
-- the L2 no-op arm's 15.2M whole-test reading is 5,759,035 marginal mem, 43.6%
of the basis, and the deposit arm's widest rung is 8,102,746.

One rung could not be built: an output whose inline datum is the empty byte
string has no descriptor at all. Pinned as an assertion, raised as an open
question, left unfixed -- this lane changes no validator code.

test(fault-proofs): point the route-freedom and #622 frontier narration at the executed rebind (#617, #622)

Doc-comment only, no assertion moves: four suites narrated the heuristic
threshold as the pre-Option-B 12,810 and the #622 pins as "not rebound here,
still with the owner". The owner ruled (b) on 2026-08-22 and the rebind to
13,522 / 14,004 executed at this wave's sign-off, so the narration points at
the executed rebind instead of the open question. Every one of these files
already read the constant rather than a literal, which is why no expectation
moved.

  min-ada-twin-cross-check-v1.test.ts     23 -> 26 tests, 0 failures
  midgard/ledger_output_proof_v1.test     8 tests | 8 passed (selector batch

The row's "778 to 784 checks in that module" figure is recorded as SUPERSEDED

docs(necessity): re-derive the §3.2 tier-1 ladder on the post-Option-B route (#617, #622)

The wave's §3.2 necessity re-derivation, run against the regenerated
blueprint. Every §3.2 artifact carried the #611 tier-1 reading — "falsified at
the signed-transaction layer above a 13,357-byte item / 13,361-byte preimage,
escalated to owner authority" — which measured the authenticate route the
complete item no longer uses. Option B (#620) moved the item to the observe
door and #622 re-measured the deployed route end-to-end, so the ladder's
tier-1 rung is re-derived:

  signed inline fit ends at a 14,004-byte item (16,369 B signed, margin 15)
  item 14,005 refused PRE-SIGN at a projected 16,385 B, auto-demoted
  the 14,336-byte cap itself stages by reference (publication 15,135 B,
    by-reference observe 1,959 B); 14,337 refuses as tier-2

Superseded figures are retained beside the new ones, as this artifact family
does for every movement it records. Tiers 2 and 3 are untouched: `K` = 15,148
reliable / 15,644 exact and the 16,613-byte tier-3 combined lower bound are
unmoved by Option B, which changed no publication and no certificate.

Files: transaction-field-chunk-v1.md (the tier table, the exact-limiting-
constraint paragraph, the no-simpler-representation paragraph and the
preserved-path paragraph), ledger-output-incremental-proof-v1.md,
native-script-traversal-v1.md, redeemer-item-traversal-v1.md,
mint-fold-asset-v1.md.

C74 is not re-measured because it has never been measured: its runner

test(validation): flip the proof-fit emulator harness onto the Option B observe door (#617, #620)

Option B (#620) made the canonical-decode item semantic transition-only, so the
authenticate stage this harness measured no longer carries the item and no
longer varies with item size. The suite's rows were measuring a stage that had
stopped being the frontier, which is why they were red after the regeneration.

Drive the full authenticate -> source -> observe journey (both validators from
parked reference scripts, per submit.ts's production shape) and measure the
observe door instead:

- the applied observe door at the staged reliability boundary, asserted
  relationally rather than by byte equality: #622 caveat 1 makes 13,522/14,004
  framing-relative to the production journey fixture family, so the exact byte
  table stays pinned only in the #622 fault-proofs suites;
- the complete signed tier-1 step transaction at the 14,336-byte preimage cap
  (#557 M2 overflow + bisect), now on observe;
- inline and reference delivery of the same item reaching identical observed
  state;
- the substituted / trailing-byte rejection row at the observe reference door,
  previously vacuous, now with an honest-publication positive control.
